newsitem.title: USA: FredMac--30-year loan top refinancing tool in 1996.
newsitem.headline: FredMac--30-year loan top refinancing tool in 1996.

text.p: The conventional 30-year fixed-rate mortgage (FRM) proved the most popular among homeowners who opted to refinance their loans in 1996, the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Association said Monday.

"Homeowners refinancing in 1996 chose new 30-year FRMs 61 percent of the time if they held a 30-year FRM, and 29 percent of the time if they held a 15-year FRM," Freddie Mac Senior Economist Vassilis Lekkas said.
Lekkas said the 29 percent rate of refinancings for 15-year FRMs last year was the highest since 1993, when it hit 30 percent.

About 43 percent of conventional mortgages originated in 1996 were refinancings, up from about 35 percent in 1995, Freddie Mac said. Eleven percent of borrowers with adjustable-rate mortgages selected a new adjustable-rate mortgage when refinancing, down from 13 percent in 1995.

Lekkas said that in general, when the cost of fixed-rate loans is low, refinancers do not choose adjustable-rate or balloon type mortgage products. Last year, 30-year FRMs rose from an average 7.03 percent in January to 8.32 percent in June, before falling to 7.60 percent in December.
Freddie Mac reported the data from a study that it conducted which is based on original and refinanced loans that it purchased.
